passages.text:
Yes, thanks everyone for the great session this morning and all the great disinfo resources overall. I think the policy piece is intimidating for a lot of field folks partly
because the subject matter on this expertise on these tech policy/governance issues among the DRG cadre is so nascent, but even for folks aware of the issues,
it's a huge operational challenge to engage -- in Ukraine it was PAS and FCS who held (and were very proprietary about) relationships with the tech platforms and
there were issues at times with our local partners' advocacy/roles vis-a-vis the interagency. Deep-dives places like BiH or Malaysia with more specifics on how

relationships.title: Quick After Action on Platform Accountability: What’s Our Role?
relationships.evidence:
[opaque block] Google Vault - Fwd: Quick After Action on Platform Accountability: What's Our Role?
- Research to see what local laws and regulations governments already have on the books (or are considering) related to platforms.
-Figure out ifanyone at your Missionalready has contacts with platforms in the country or the region where you work.
- Identify local civil society organizations who are already working to hold platforms more accountable.
- Support existing or new forums that bring together government, civil society and platforms to discuss platform governance.
- What else am I missing? In terms of low-hanging fruit to get people started?
+ Nadereh and Adam, please chime in too based on your experience. In case this is useful for future sessions on the Disinformation Primer and also for us at
OTI since our projects have smaller timeframes and budgets.
Best,
Amy Noreuil Malessa
Senior Digital Technology Advisor for Field Programs Division
Bureau for Conflict Prevention and Stabilization | Office of Transition Initiatives | Creative Digital Team
US Agency for International Development
